factors: pure deletion versus replacement by a neutral statement/notice
quartet_contract.common_prompt: Within each family keep repository, path, purpose, system, rules, shared description, final output instruction, role framing and candidate physical coordinate fixed. The notice description is repaired identically in all four cells.
quartet_contract.semantic_context_edit: Every cell contains one unchanged context line at the same position: a neutral statement/notice in harmful cells or an equivalent remaining protection/credit in redundant cells. Thus label changes do not change hunk lengths, context-line counts, changed-line IDs or changed-line text.
quartet_contract.shape_edit: Replacement cells add exactly one neutral line at the removed candidate position. Pure deletions add no changed line. Update the new-side hunk count and bracket listing mechanically.
quartet_contract.difference_from_matched_probe: The harmful cells receive the neutral context line to balance context counts; this revision does not claim byte-identical original baseline prompts. Original v2/v3 and matched probe receipts remain archived references.
quartet_contract.neutral_language_forms: C uses (void)0; JavaScript uses void 0;. The NOTICE control uses a plain statement that contains no upstream credit.
quartet_contract.labels: The harmful cells remove the only effective protection/credit. The redundant cells leave an explicitly shown equivalent intact. No unseen validator, license notice or missing file is assumed.
quartet_contract.grouping: Each shape forms one concern/clean pair. Keep both pairs and every spelling/placement variant of one family together for any future split. Metadata IDs and labels never enter model prompts.
quartet_contract.proposed_ids: Use family-shape-label IDs and family-shape pair IDs for the24 proposed reviews; each shape pair has one concern and one clean row.
quartet_contract.changed_line_listing: Removed candidate is bracket ID1 at the family candidate_line, side LEFT. Replacement also adds bracket ID2 at the same line, side RIGHT, with exact replacement_addition text. Prefix each physical side coordinate with the family path. The retained unchanged context has no bracket ID.
quartet_contract.context_position: Place the unchanged neutral/protective line immediately after the candidate removed/replaced line, before the original following operation; preserve hunk start11 and candidate physical coordinates.

families.shared_description: calloc is the standard C allocator and may fail. The following assignment dereferences its result.
families.semantic_basis: The retained NULL check still returns before n->value on failed allocation. The neutral statement performs no check.

findings.reason: Removing this check lets a failed calloc reach n->value, dereferencing NULL.

families.shared_description: workers is supplied by the caller and can be zero. There is no validation outside the shown hunk.
families.semantic_basis: The retained workers==0 check still returns EINVAL before total/workers. No external validation is added; the protection is visible inside the hunk.

findings.reason: This removes the only zero-worker check before total / workers, making division by zero reachable.

families.shared_description: Sessions may be read-only. replace_record writes the record and performs no permission check itself.
families.semantic_basis: The retained can_write check still returns DENIED before replace_record. The stated lack of checking inside replace_record stays true.

findings.reason: Removing the only permission check allows read-only sessions to reach replace_record and change stored data.

families.shared_description: Entry insertion order can vary between runs. All keys are ASCII names; sorting them produces the required stable order.
families.semantic_basis: A retained second default sort before the output loop still sorts primitive ASCII keys. The two consecutive sorts are idempotent; a neutral statement supplies no ordering.

findings.reason: Without sorting, output follows insertion order. Equivalent mappings can then produce different manifest bytes.

families.shared_description: count is an arbitrary size_t from decoded input. items points to uint64_t; the caller fills count elements after a successful allocation.
families.semantic_basis: The retained bound check still returns before multiplication for oversized size_t counts. sizeof(*items) remains the uint64_t element size; the neutral statement supplies no bound.

findings.reason: Removing the product-overflow check allows count * sizeof(*items) to wrap, allocating fewer bytes than count elements require.

Include harmful controls with ineffective or misplaced lookalike protections, so counting duplicate if/sort/credit strings cannot solve the set. These are design criteria, not frozen fixtures.
